title: Trump and Putin to Hold Surprise One-on-One Talks at Asia Summit
snippet: President Donald Trump will meet privately with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, marking their first direct summit in over a year amid ongoing fighting in Ukraine.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump is set to hold a high-stakes, one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of an Asia summit, a U.S. official confirmed. The unexpected face-to-face gathering marks the first direct interaction between the two leaders in over a year.

The bilateral session was not initially listed on Trump's official travel schedule. The president was already scheduled to participate in a trilateral meeting alongside Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss nuclear disarmament, trade, and the conflict in Iran. However, the Kremlin announced the separate 1-on-1 talks prior to the White House's official confirmation.

A Changing Diplomatic Landscape

While the White House has not formally released an agenda for the private meeting, Trump told reporters on Monday that he intends to address Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine. The direct dialogue with leaders from Moscow and Beijing underscores the administration's continued pivot away from standard diplomatic norms and traditional international alliances.

The two leaders last met in person in Anchorage, Alaska, in August 2025. Although that summit concluded without any formal agreement or ceasefire, Trump has maintained an optimistic stance regarding a potential resolution to the war.

Rhetoric Versus Reality

Speaking to reporters earlier this week, Trump suggested that the Russian leader might be shifting his posture in Ukraine. "I think he could be tougher, frankly," Trump said. "I think he’s backing down a little bit."

Despite Trump's assessment, violence on the ground remains severe as the conflict enters its fifth year. Russian forces have launched a steady stream of drone and missile attacks leading up to Thursday's summit, while Ukrainian forces recently damaged a vital bridge connecting the Crimean Peninsula to the Russian mainland.
